title: Tissue Quality Evaluation for Brain Perfusion/Dissection Specimens
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
materials: Tissue Quality Evaluation for Brain Perfusion/Dissection Specimens
See Vivarium Entry Procedures and Movement Between Rooms
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) should always be used while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what PPE you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
AF0061 Brain Dissection of Post-natal mice
AF0075 Mouse Cardiac Perfusion Fixation and Brain Collection
Damaged or missing olfactory bulbs and/or paraflocculi.
Tissue has been nicked or removed.

steps.title: Monitor Perfusion Process
steps.instruction: Observe the animal during the perfusion sequence to evaluate the effectiveness of the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Verify that the liver clears and turns an ashen grey color after the right atrium is clipped and saline is pumped into the left ventricle.
Observe for PFA reaction: tail flicking, violent muscle twitching, and intestinal expansion (internal organs expanding and protruding).
Confirm post-perfusion stiffness of the entire body, including extremities and internal organs.
Ensure lungs remain pink and not inflated, and that no solutions dripped from the nose or mouth.

steps.title: Evaluate Harvested Brain Quality
steps.instruction: Inspect the harvested brain for perfusion quality and physical damage.

substeps.instruction: Verify the brain has an all-around dull cream color and the brain stem is white.
Confirm that veins are no longer visible on the surface of the brain.
Check for blushiness (red/pink spots) to distinguish from transgenic expression (which is typically uniform/symmetrical).
Inspect for tool, dura, or bone damage, specifically looking for slices/grazing into the tissue where no tissue was removed.

steps.title: Assess Dissection Damage
steps.instruction: Perform a detailed inspection of all sides and structures of the brain to identify dissection-related damage, noting that fresh (non-fixed) tissue is softer and more prone to damage.

substeps.instruction: Identify slices into the tissue from tools, dura, or bone.
Identify nicks where chunks of tissue have been removed.
Check if olfactory bulbs or cerebellum are stretched or disrupted and no longer match the cortex.

steps.title: Assign Quality Classification
steps.instruction: Categorize the specimen as Perfect, Good, Fair, or Poor based on the following criteria:

substeps.instruction: Perfect: Liver cleared well (not red); lungs pinkish-red and not inflated; strong PFA reaction; body stiff; brain firm with no red/pink spots; vessels cleared; no dissection damage; 1-2 mm of brain stem intact.

Good: Liver cleared well (tips of lobes may be slightly red); lungs normal color but slightly inflated; no solution from mouth/nose; visible PFA reaction; body stiff; brain firm with no red/pink spots; vessels cleared; may have missing paraflocculus or slight bone fragment disruption to olfactory bulbs; brain stem may be < 1-2 mm but no dissection damage.

Fair: Limited PFA reaction (tail flexing only); liver cleared but some lobes red/splotchy; body slightly stiff; lungs slightly inflated with slow solution leak from nose; slight pink area on cerebellum (no vessels showing); tissue grazed during dissection (no tissue removed); both paraflocculi may be missing; brain stem damaged or < 1-2 mm.

Poor: Liver did not clear; no/slight PFA reaction; body not stiff; lungs bright white and inflated with solution from nose/mouth; brain not firm; visible vessels or pink spots; tissue removed or sliced by dura/tools; both paraflocculi and/or olfactory bulbs missing; severe brain stem damage or missing; cerebellum separated from cortex; tissue loss in cortex, cerebellum, or brain stem.
